Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Procurement team provides services to the businesses that are the backbone of Stripe. Stripe’s broader Procurement organization consists of Third Party Risk, Strategic Sourcing, Supplier Deal Management (Procurement Contracting), Procurement Enablement, Accounts Payable, and Travel and Expense.

Our Procurement Contracting function, Supplier Deal Management (SDM), builds an efficient supplier contracting process, reduces friction for business leaders, works in partnership with Third Party Risk and Legal to minimize risk, and increases the speed at which Stripe can engage key suppliers.

SDM’s mission is to drive agreements efficiently through appropriate channels, bringing structure to the overall contracting process in partnership with stakeholders while providing a customized and guided user experience and effectively managing value and risk for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Reporting to the Head of SDM and working closely with SDM Leads, you’ll support the supplier contracting process, from answering initial questions and reviewing use cases to negotiating commercial terms and supporting contract lifecycle management.

Responsibilities 

  • Answer initial questions and educate directly responsible individuals (DRIs) on the overall risk assessment and supplier contracting process
  • Conduct an initial review of DRI-provided use cases and appropriate contractual terms, or assemble appropriate Stripe templates, and prepare agreements for legal review according to defined guidelines when necessary
  • Review and negotiate commercial terms in supplier agreements when needed
  • Monitor productivity and communication with DRIs using our procurement tool, Zip
  • Engage internal stakeholders, including Legal, Sourcing, Third Party Risk, and Stripe DRIs, to understand their needs and translate them into a risk-balanced approach to preparing contracts using training and existing frameworks
  • Manage engagements within our procurement system, Zip, and contract lifecycle management system, Ironclad, and support end-to-end contract lifecycle management
  • Partner with respective internal teams to resolve business inquiries and troubleshoot issues related to contracting

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 8 years of professional experience in contracting within procurement, legal operations, or another commercial deal negotiation capacity
  • Demonstrated ability to understand commercial and legal language commonly used in commercial contracts, ease in reviewing and drafting contractual language, and experience negotiating contracts and partnering effectively with legal teams
  • A solution-oriented mindset with enthusiasm for establishing contracting best practices, the ability to earn trust quickly and deliver value for a critical, fast-paced function involving multiple stakeholders, and the ability to support opinions with sound reasoning
  • Flexibility and comfort with changing requirements in a high-volume environment, meticulous attention to detail, and a rigorous decision-making process
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to represent Stripe effectively when interacting with stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

  • Broad contracting experience across a range of common categories, such as technology, marketing, workplace, and services
  • Understanding of or experience with e-procurement tools and contract lifecycle management systems, such as Zip and Ironclad
  • Familiarity with the fintech industry and its supply chain and procurement challenges
  • A builder’s mindset and a willingness to question assumptions and conventional wisdom

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

Build and lead growth across Kamino’s direct and partner-distributed financial products.

The role

Kamino is hiring a Head of Growth to turn our direct and partner-distributed financial products into sustained growth in funded customers, retained capital and revenue. You will own the growth strategy across acquisition, activation, retention and cross-product adoption, deciding where to invest and which approaches can scale.

This is a hands-on function-building role. You will own the budget, establish measurement and launch the foundational programs before hiring the team to expand them. Your remit includes lifecycle, referrals, partner distribution and paid acquisition—not a single channel or discipline.

Success means customers put capital to work, stay active and generate lasting value after acquisition and incentive costs.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and lead the Growth function. Own strategy, budget and forecasts across direct and partner-distributed products. Launch the foundational programs yourself, then hire the team to scale them.

  • Acquire funded customers. Build paid acquisition alongside other high-potential channels. Own channel economics, creative testing and conversion across marketing-controlled journeys.

  • Build lifecycle and retention. Establish the CRM, automation and customer programs that drive repeat use, cross-product adoption, retained capital and reactivation.

  • Activate partner distribution. Work with Business Development and partners to turn access through wallets, exchanges and financial applications into funded customer activity and revenue.

  • Invest against measurable results. Own attribution and experimentation. Allocate spending and incentives based on customer quality, incremental growth and payback—including whether activity lasts after rewards end.

What you bring

  • 10+ years of growth experience, including senior ownership of growth for a D2C financial product and direct experience serving U.S. customers.

  • A record of growing funded customers, retained balances, repeat activity or revenue while maintaining strong acquisition economics and customer quality.

  • Experience building a Growth function in a lean company: setting direction, doing the foundational work personally, and hiring and developing the team that scaled it.

  • The ability to lead across acquisition and lifecycle, with deep expertise in at least one of paid acquisition or lifecycle and the judgment to hire strong specialists. Paid acquisition is one part of the broader growth remit.

  • Experience building CRM and lifecycle systems using segmentation, automation and controlled experiments, and improving conversion across campaign journeys, landing pages, referrals and other marketing-controlled surfaces.

  • Ownership of material growth budgets, with strong judgment across attribution, incrementality, cohort quality, customer value, payback and forecasting. You allocate investment according to customer quality and channel economics.

  • Sound judgment around customer trust, compliance and platform policies, and clear executive communication across Marketing, Product, Design, Data, Finance and Business Development.

  • Daily fluency with AI tools and workflows that improve the speed and quality of your work.

STRONGLY PREFERRED

  • Direct experience growing crypto, digital-asset or onchain products.

  • Experience with financial products where growth depends on funded balances and repeat transactions.

  • Experience growing products through another company’s customer experience.

  • Experience building growth across a connected portfolio of financial products.

Working at Kamino

You will work directly with senior leadership. You will partner with Product Marketing and Brand on the campaigns customers see. You will work with Product, Design, and Product Data where acquisition and lifecycle journeys meet the product. Business Development will bring new distribution routes into the growth portfolio. This is a full-time role based in New York City. We work together in the office four days per week. Kamino may provide immigration sponsorship for an exceptional candidate who meets the experience bar and can work from New York.

Compensation and benefits

The expected annual base salary range for this role is USD $210,000–$260,000. Kamino expects to offer a competitive package consisting of base salary, a performance-based bonus and long-term KMNO participation.

Final terms will reflect the candidate’s relevant experience, skills and agreed scope of the role.

Benefits and applicable employment terms will be documented as part of the formal offer.

Kamino is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building an inclusive workplace. Kamino does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

About Hashgraph:

Hashgraph is a fast-growing software company committed to supporting, developing and servicing Hedera, an open source, proof-of-stake platform. Hedera is EVM-compatible and has been specifically built to meet the needs of enterprise and web3 applications, which require speed, security, stability and sustainability. Hedera’s public network is governed by industry-leading organizations, spanning 11 sectors and 14 regions who oversee the development and direction of the decentralized platform.

Why this role exists:

Assets are landing on ledgers faster than anyone has built a way to move them between ledgers. Collateral sits on one chain while the position it should be margining sits on another. Delivery-versus-payment and payment-versus-payment both work inside a single ledger and both break the moment the two legs live in different places. The available workarounds are bridges, which have lost more than $2.8 billion since 2021.

The team that built Hedera from the ground up is now building a cross-ledger solution for institutional settlement: collateral mobility, DvP, PvP, cross-border payments, and FX across public and private ledgers that do not otherwise interoperate.

Your job will be to define the product and own the roadmap. You will report to the founder.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and roadmap.

  • Work closely with business development on go-to-market execution for the product. Define the product the market needs and business development can sell..

  • Report product status and roadmap changes directly to the founders and executive team.

  • Design and run trials with external validators, partners, and customers.

  • Make the release readiness call on performance, security, and usability. Ask the tough questions before launch, not after.

  • Run program management across every stakeholder group. Keep BD, Marketing, and Engineering in sync.

What success looks like in 12 months:

  • Live settlement for the priority use cases of cross-border payments, settlements, treasury management, and tokenized deposits, with named institutional counterparties moving real value.

  • You will have built working on/off-ramps supporting the use cases above.

  • BD, marketing, and engineering each independently say you are the reason they are shipping faster.

What you bring:

Core capabilities:

  • 10+ years in product management, product leadership, or an equivalent operating role.

  • 5+ years of that inside FX, payments, settlement, clearing, custody, collateral management, or banking infrastructure.

  • Real operating experience in FX exchange, payments, settlement, or banking-rail businesses. You understand cross-border payments, stablecoins, on/off-ramps, and how players like SWIFT and Stripe fit together.

  • Direct working knowledge of at least two of: FX execution and settlement, cross-border payments, DvP or PvP settlement, collateral mobility, treasury operations, tokenized deposits.

Functional expertise:

  • Experience owning a roadmap end to end, including making the right, hard calls.

  • Experience writing product requirements that an engineering team built from directly.

  • Experience presenting to executives, boards, or institutional steering committees.

Preferred skills and experience:

  • Distributed ledger or Layer 1 experience.

  • Work inside a consortium, governing council, or member-owned network model.

  • Exposure to CCIP, Circle and ARC, Canton, Ripple, or comparable enterprise platforms.

  • Stablecoin mechanics, on-ramps and off-ramps, tokenized collateral.

  • First product hire or zero-to-one experience at an early-stage company.

Candidates who meet the basic qualifications and none of the preferred should still apply. The preferred list is learnable in a quarter.

Travel to customer, validator, and partner sites, including international travel will be required.

Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

You Will

  • Help build out infrastructure that gives us better inventory of our network edge security posture
  • Build out and maintain a near-real time streaming analytics data pipeline and application

You should be comfortable designing flows yourself, building interactive prototypes, and working through interaction details with designers and engineers. You’ll also own the product decisions: which customer problem to solve, what to ship first, and how to measure whether the experience improved.

The opportunity

  • Design complete social journeys. Work through how someone discovers a person, decides to follow them, shares an idea or trade, receives a response, and returns. Connect these interactions into an experience users understand without explanation.

  • Make the interaction details work. Shape navigation, information hierarchy, copy, defaults, gestures, and feedback. Specify what happens when a feed is empty, a post fails, content loads slowly, or someone changes their mind.

  • Prototype before committing to a build. Turn ideas into interactive prototypes that communicate the intended behavior. Explore alternatives, test the uncertain parts, and give engineering clear flows, states, and acceptance criteria.

  • Use psychology to improve participation. Understand why people hesitate to post, seek recognition, follow strangers, or respond to others. Translate those motivations into decisions about audience visibility, prompts, reputation, feedback, and the effort required to contribute.

  • Observe users and fix what gets in their way. Run usability sessions, watch people complete tasks, and combine those observations with funnel data. Identify where people misunderstand the product, lose confidence, or abandon an action.

  • Design for first use and repeated use. Make the experience useful before someone has connections. Keep sharing lightweight during an active trading session, with clear control over what becomes public. Test the twentieth interaction as carefully as the first.

  • Connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. For each significant change, define the expected behavior and how to test it. Track task completion, abandonment, first follows, first contributions, responses, and subsequent retention. Work with data science to evaluate experiments and effects on both contributors and their audiences.

  • Take the experience through launch. Choose a focused initial scope, resolve trade-offs with engineering, review the implementation against the intended design, and use post-launch evidence to decide what to improve next.

What you bring

  • Has designed and shipped consumer social experiences. Your portfolio shows your contribution to feeds, profiles, sharing, messaging, discovery, or communities—and how the experience changed after launch.

  • Has strong interaction design craft. You can explain why a flow is structured a particular way, what users will notice first, what they need to understand, and which decisions or steps can be removed.

About the Team

The Security team is responsible for and committed to securing all things at TRM. From our customers to our code, and everything in between, the security team is involved in all aspects of the business. As a Senior Cloud Security Engineer, you will lead the charter for maturing TRM’s cloud infrastructure and security systems at scale. From designing the strategy to implementing best practices, your work will accelerate our mission of building a safer financial system for billions of people.

The impact you will have here:

  • Provide technical guidance and leadership as a cybersecurity expert on topics such as architecture, configuration management, and environment design

  • Leverage automation tools, configuration management, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) solutions to standardize security across all environments

  • Guide relevant stakeholders such as engineering, product, and leadership and ensure alignment with security strategies

  • Identify and communicate cloud platform vulnerabilities and mitigation options to stakeholders that balance business agility with security

  • Relevant industry experience in managing cloud security programs, Identity Access Management (IAM), and cloud-native security solutions (e.g., firewalls)

  • Strong bias for action; ability to juggle multiple priorities and create a sense of urgency in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

  • Transparency is at the heart of how we operate, both within the team and with the business, as we focus on clearly communicating and addressing cyber risks.

  • Eastern Standard Time (EST - GMT-4)

  • Pacific Standard Time (PST - GMT-7)

  • Prioritize Rapid Threat Assessments: Efficiently perform security risk assessments and triage vulnerabilities based on immediate risk to the business, focusing on the most critical issues with minimal delays.

  • Integrate Security Early in Development: Embed security testing and reviews within our Product Shipping Framework and CI/CD pipelines to ensure that security is automated and runs parallel to the fast-paced development cycle, preventing bottlenecks.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.
